title: Near-atomistic simulations reveal the molecular principles that control chromatin structure and phase separation
task: Simulate chromatin structure and phase separation at near-atomistic resolution
key_results: OpenCGChromatin models fibers up to 108 nucleosomes (~kilobase scale); predicts linker-DNA-dependent structures matching cryo-ET data; identifies H4K16 and H3K9 acetylation as most disruptive modifications for chromatin compaction
comments: Bridging molecular detail to mesoscale chromatin organization is valuable, though experimental validation of predicted histone-tail interaction networks remains indirect.

model_io.model: OpenCGChromatin coarse-grained molecular dynamics

hypotheses.hypothesis: Linker-DNA length controls histone tail accessibility and condensate structure
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: simulations independently predict observed cryo-ET structures and biochemical stability

hypotheses.hypothesis: Acetylation disrupts compaction in a pattern-specific manner via tail-mediated interactions
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: H4K16 and H3K9 modifications show greatest energetic disruption

title: The structural dynamics and molecular coupling in the slow inactivation of a prokaryotic voltage-gated sodium channel
task: Elucidate slow inactivation mechanism and structural coupling in voltage-gated sodium channels
key_results: smFRET identifies three conformational states of NavAb selectivity filter; L176-T206 residue pair forms steric-hindrance coupler mediating slow inactivation; L176F mutation restores high FRET population disrupted by S6 deletion or lidocaine
comments: Single-molecule FRET combined with crystallography elegantly maps conformational states, though functional validation of the proposed L176-T206 'conformational talk' mechanism could be strengthened with electrophysiology.

model_io.model: smFRET spectroscopy on NavAb selectivity filter
inputs: NavAb wild-type and mutants (L176F, T206A, ΔC230)

model_io.model: X-ray crystallography

hypotheses.hypothesis: Selectivity filter is the slow inactivation gate undergoing depolarization-dependent conformational changes
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: depolarization enriches high FRET state consistent with inactivated conformation

hypotheses.hypothesis: L176-T206 coupling mediates primary-to-inactivation gate communication
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: L176F overrides S6 deletion effects; T206A partially uncouples gates

title: Wild-type and mutated ß-catenin differently repress RND3/RHOE expression in hepatocellular carcinoma
task: Characterize β-catenin-mediated repression of RND3 expression in hepatocellular carcinoma
key_results: Wild-type β-catenin suppresses RND3 via Hippo pathway; oncogenic β-catenin downregulates RND3 through miR-512-3p targeting 3'UTR
comments: The parallel repression mechanisms—one transcriptional (Hippo) and one post-transcriptional (miR-512-3p)—provide mechanistic elegance but require validation of functional consequences for HCC behavior.

model_io.model: Human HCC samples and cultured cell lines

hypotheses.hypothesis: Both structural and transcriptional functions of β-catenin repress RND3 expression through distinct pathways
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: wild-type via Hippo pathway suppression; oncogenic via miR-512-3p-mediated 3'UTR targeting

title: p300/CBP inhibition promotes apoptosis in mouse embryos by impairing H1K75ac-associated DNA repair during the 4-cell-to-blastocyst transition
task: Determine role of p300/CBP in DNA repair and apoptosis during mouse preimplantation embryo development
key_results: p300/CBP inhibition reduced blastocyst formation rates, increased DNA damage accumulation, and promoted apoptosis via impaired ATM-mediated DNA repair and reduced H1K75ac
comments: The mechanistic link between H1K75ac loss and ATM dysfunction provides a specific epigenetic-DNA damage axis relevant to developmental competence, though causality requires further validation.

model_io.model: Mouse 4-cell to blastocyst transition with p300/CBP inhibition

hypotheses.hypothesis: p300/CBP inhibition impairs embryonic development through reduced H1K75ac-associated DNA repair
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: p300/CBP inhibition reduced H1K75ac, impaired ATM response, and increased DNA damage and apoptosis

title: The FOS transcription factor negatively regulates MAFF to control myometrial cell contractility
task: Determine FOS-mediated regulation of MAFF and its role in myometrial contractility
key_results: FOS occupies MAFF promoter and negatively regulates MAFF; MAFF-deficient cells show 15–25% reduced basal contractility; MAFF overexpression increased contraction by 4–8%
comments: The modest contractile changes (4–8%) and variable responses among MAFF-deficient clones suggest MAFF is one component of a complex contractility network requiring additional regulators.

model_io.model: Human myometrial cells with FOS/MAFF manipulation

hypotheses.hypothesis: FOS negatively regulates MAFF expression and MAFF contributes to myometrial contractility
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: FOS knockdown increased MAFF ~1.5–1.7-fold; MAFF deficiency reduced contractility; MAFF overexpression increased contraction

title: Fresh frozen plasma-based resuscitation lessens lung injury in mice with abdominal sepsis and hemorrhagic shock
task: Evaluate FFP vs fibrinogen resuscitation effects on endothelial syndecan-1 and lung injury in combined sepsis-hemorrhagic shock
key_results: FFP significantly attenuated CLP+HS-induced alveolar thickening and syndecan-1 shedding; fibrinogen provided no protection despite restoring shed blood volume
comments: Fibrinogen's failure to match FFP efficacy suggests additional plasma components beyond fibrinogen are critical for endothelial protection, warranting investigation of other plasma factors.

model_io.model: C57BL/6 mice with cecal ligation/puncture + hemorrhagic shock

hypotheses.hypothesis: FFP and fibrinogen would attenuate CLP+HS-induced endothelial injury and syndecan-1 shedding
hypotheses.result: FFP attenuated injury; fibrinogen did not, suggesting FFP contains protective factors beyond fibrinogen

title: PRKACA modulates endoplasmic reticulum stress-associated dysfunction in granulosa cell models relevant to polycystic ovary syndrome
task: Identify PRKACA's role in ER stress-associated granulosa cell dysfunction in PCOS
key_results: PRKACA knockdown reduced CREB phosphorylation, CYP19A1, and BCL2 while increasing GRP78, CHOP, and apoptosis; 4-PBA partially reversed effects; PRKACA overexpression attenuated tunicamycin-induced ER stress
comments: Heterogeneous PRKACA expression across public cohorts and lack of FDR-corrected significance suggest context-dependent dysregulation; functional studies support a protective role regardless of baseline expression variance.

model_io.model: KGN and SVOG granulosa-lineage cells; primary granulosa cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: PRKACA modulates ER stress-associated granulosa cell dysfunction in PCOS
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: PRKACA knockdown increased ER stress markers and apoptosis; overexpression attenuated tunicamycin-induced stress and preserved steroid production

title: The long non-coding RNA LINC00276-202 regulates RPE differentiation through hnRNPL and β-catenin-associated signaling
task: Elucidate LINC00276-202 regulation of RPE cell differentiation through miRNA and protein interactions
key_results: LINC00276-202 silencing reduced RPE differentiation genes (RPE65, MITF, TRPM1/3); miR-204/211-responsive region contributes to function; hnRNPL interaction modulates β-catenin levels and TCF/LEF activity
comments: The model integrates miRNA-responsiveness and protein-binding partners, though the functional hierarchy between miR-204/211-responsive region and hnRNPL-β-catenin axis remains incompletely defined.

model_io.model: ARPE-19 human retinal pigment epithelial cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: LINC00276-202 regulates RPE differentiation through miR-204/211-responsive region, hnRNPL interaction, and β-catenin signaling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: silencing reduced differentiation genes; miR-responsive region and hnRNPL binding both contribute; hnRNPL modulates β-catenin and TCF/LEF activity

title: Harnessing cell cycle synchronization to boost the therapeutic potential of umbilical cord MSCs against acute colitis
task: Optimize UCMSC therapeutic efficacy for acute colitis by cell cycle synchronization
key_results: G0/G1-synchronized UCMSCs achieved ~80–90% enrichment; S-phase ~60% enrichment; synchronized cells (not specific phase) significantly reduced colon shortening (vs DSS control) and inflammatory infiltration; 15–25% improvement in disease outcomes
comments: The finding that synchronization-per-se rather than specific phases enhanced efficacy suggests the pretreatment/selection process itself (enriching homogeneous populations) may be therapeutically valuable independent of cell cycle state.

model_io.model: Human UCMSCs with DSS-induced acute colitis in mice

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cell cycle synchronization enhances UCMSC therapeutic efficacy against acute colitis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: synchronized UCMSCs (not specific phase) significantly attenuated DSS-induced colon shortening and inflammatory infiltration relative to non-synchronized controls

title: LMOD2 attenuates Ang II-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy by activating the Nrf2-mediated antioxidant pathway
task: Elucidate LMOD2-mediated protection against Ang II-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy
key_results: LMOD2 overexpression attenuated hypertrophic markers (ANP, BNP, MYH7) and reduced oxidative stress through Nrf2 pathway activation; Nrf2 inhibitor ML385 abolished protection
comments: The dependence on Nrf2 is cleanly demonstrated through pharmacological rescue/inhibition experiments, though LMOD2's upstream mechanism for Nrf2 activation remains unclear.

model_io.model: H9c2 cardiomyocytes with Ang II stimulation

hypotheses.hypothesis: LMOD2 suppresses Ang II-induced hypertrophy by activating Nrf2-mediated antioxidant signaling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: LMOD2 overexpression promoted Nrf2 nuclear accumulation and antioxidant gene expression; Nrf2 inhibitor abrogated LMOD2 protection

title: Switches in alternatively spliced isoforms impact protein and drug interactions in melanoma, ovarian cancer, and acute myeloid leukemia
task: Identifying switches in alternatively spliced isoforms affecting protein/drug interactions in cancer
key_results: Most Dominant Transcript (MDT) switching between normal and cancer samples disrupts protein interaction networks
comments: Abstract truncated; full results and specific cancer findings unclear from provided text.

model_io.model: Alternative splicing analysis with isoform switching detection
inputs: RNA-Seq from melanoma, ovarian cancer, acute myeloid leukemia samples

hypotheses.hypothesis: Switches in predominantly expressed isoforms disrupt protein interaction networks and drive tumor progression
hypotheses.result: Confirmed in three cancer types; MDT switching identified as potential diagnostic and therapeutic target

title: Long-read sequencing with targeted assembly of the opsin locus accurately evaluates genes in expressed positions
task: Long-read nanopore sequencing with targeted assembly for accurate opsin gene analysis and color vision deficiency diagnosis
key_results: Targeted assembly achieved 99% concordance for OPN1LW and 92% for OPN1MW copy numbers; resolved gene order in 100% of XY and 87% of XX individuals; detected 3.2% CVD prevalence in XY, 8% carriers in XX
comments: Assembly-based approach superior to alignment-based methods but 87% resolution in XX individuals suggests technical challenges in highly repetitive regions.

model_io.model: Nanopore long-read sequencing + targeted de novo assembly

hypotheses.hypothesis: Targeted assembly enables accurate CVD diagnosis in complex repetitive loci resistant to alignment-based methods
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; assembly-based approach resolved gene order and detected population-concordant CVD prevalence; carrier detection improved in XX individuals

title: Interpretable survival prediction in Parkinson’s disease with AI-assisted web deployment
task: Survival prediction in Parkinson's disease using Cox regression and machine learning with temporal validation
key_results: Cox, random survival forest, XGBoost achieved mean C-index 0.716; temporal validation C-index 0.708; 2-, 4-, 6-year AUCs 0.713, 0.726, 0.750 on deployed Cox model
comments: Reproducible web-based tool with strong discrimination but modest calibration (modest underestimation of absolute mortality); external validation in independent PD registry recommended.

model_io.model: Cox proportional hazards regression + machine learning ensemble (random survival forest, XGBoost)
inputs: 11 predictors: demographic, genetic, treatment, motor, non-motor domains

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multiple predictors spanning demographic, genetic, and clinical domains enable accurate PD survival prediction
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; Cox model discrimination comparable to tree-based methods with better interpretability for clinical deployment

title: A blockchain-based non-fungible tokens framework for ownership and intellectual property preserving with controlled access to medical datasets
task: Blockchain-based NFT framework for medical dataset ownership, IP protection, and controlled access
key_results: Merkle-tree construction 0.0073 ± 0.0006 s for 3,151 files; AES-256 decryption 0.33 ± 0.05 ms per file; NFT deployment 417,023 gas on Polygon testnet
comments: Architecture is computationally feasible but incomplete implementation (missing on-chain approval, revocation, recovery); watermark vulnerable to geometric transforms; legal status of NFT-based ownership claims uncertain.

model_io.model: MedNFT-Gov (blockchain governance with encrypted off-chain storage)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Blockchain NFTs with cryptographic integrity commitment enable provenance tracking and controlled access
hypotheses.result: Confirmed in proof-of-concept; full production deployment requires auxiliary key management and legal framework

title: CrossCD-Eval: a unified framework with domain-aware feature normalization for cross-domain remote sensing change detection
task: Cross-domain change detection in remote sensing with domain-aware feature normalization
key_results: DAFN improves cross-domain and few-shot adaptation performance; reduces IoU standard deviation by up to 22.7%; outperforms preprocessing, AdaBN, adversarial feature alignment
comments: DAFN is lightweight and effective, but gains primarily on challenging source-target shifts; application limited to change detection rather than other remote sensing tasks.

model_io.model: Domain-Aware Feature Normalization (DAFN) module applied to GLAFormer, Change-Mamba, EHCTNet, ELGC-Net, STNet
inputs: remote sensing image pairs from different domains (CLCD, HRSCD, LEVIR-CD)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Feature-level domain adaptation via statistic alignment improves cross-domain change detection
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; DAFN improves adaptation performance and stability under challenging domain shifts; gains independent of preprocessing confounds

title: AMF-U-Net: an adaptive multimodal fusion residual attention 3D U-Net for boundary-aware brain tumour segmentation
task: 3D segmentation of brain tumors from multimodal MRI using adaptive multimodal fusion and attention
key_results: AMF-U-Net achieves Dice 0.845 (WT), 0.813 (TC), 0.788 (ET); macro-average Dice 0.815; outperforms 3D U-Net, nnU-Net, UNETR, Swin UNETR on boundary metrics
comments: Modality importance weighting via softmax-normalized attention is intuitive, but ablation study lacking to isolate contributions of residual connections, attention gates, and fusion module.

model_io.model: AMF-U-Net (multi-stream 3D U-Net with Modality Fusion Module and attention gates)
inputs: T1, T1ce, T2, FLAIR MRI volumes
outputs: tumor segmentation mask (background, necrotic, edema, enhancing tumor)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adaptive modality fusion improves multi-scale feature extraction and boundary reconstruction
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; AMF-U-Net shows superior overlap and boundary distance metrics

title: Small molecules targeting ARF1 interaction with C9orf72:SMCR8:WDR41 complexes suppress its overactivation implicated in ALS/FTD
task: Identifying small molecules that suppress ARF1 overactivation in ALS/FTD
key_results: SCC944 identified as ARF1-CSW modulator; binds directly to ARF1 and reduces GTP-bound ARF1; produces brefeldin A-like Golgi/microtubule/mitochondrial reorganization with distinct protein trafficking
comments: In vitro binding and cellular assays are promising but in vivo efficacy in ALS/FTD models and human safety data absent.

model_io.model: Computer-aided rational drug design + high-throughput in-silico screening

hypotheses.hypothesis: ARF1 modulation via CSW interaction is therapeutic for ALS/FTD
hypotheses.result: Partially confirmed; SCC944 demonstrates brefeldin A-like effects but clinical translation requires in vivo validation

title: Fundamental dynamical units for physics-informed structural inference from perturbation time-series in networked systems
task: Structural inference of signed interaction networks from perturbation time-series data
key_results: Fundamental Dynamical Units (FDUs) reduce interaction hypothesis space to finite, tractable representation; physics-informed neural ODE enables joint recovery of structure and trajectories
comments: FDU formalism elegantly addresses combinatorial complexity but validation limited to synthetic benchmarks with known ground truth.

model_io.model: Physics-informed neural ODE with FDU regularization

hypotheses.hypothesis: Local interaction structure determines perturbation conditions needed to disentangle direct from relayed influence
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; FDU representation converts structural hypotheses into verifiable dynamical predictions

title: Artificial intelligence driven multimodal medical image segmentation algorithm: applied research and clinical verification
task: Multimodal medical image segmentation for CT, MRI, and PET across multiple organs
key_results: AMIS-Net achieves Dice 0.8317 on Synapse; reduces radiologist reading time from 8.5 to 4.2 min (senior) and 12.3 to 5.7 min (junior); improves diagnostic accuracy
comments: Clinical validation on liver tumors and intracranial hemorrhage is encouraging, but proprietary dataset limits external reproducibility assessment.

model_io.model: AMIS-Net (encoder-decoder with Dual Attention Module and Small Object Capture module)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adaptive feature recalibration and multi-scale feature extraction improve cross-modal segmentation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; AMIS-Net outperforms U-Net, ResUNet, and STUNet on CHAOS and Synapse benchmarks

title: Comparative genomics of Helicobacter pylori isolated from liver fluke endemic regions in Thailand
task: Comparative genomics and virulence profiling of Helicobacter pylori from liver fluke-endemic Thailand
key_results: 14 isolates predominantly Southeast Asian lineage; all carried cagA with Western-type (ABC), East Asian-type (ABD), and non-canonical EPIYA motifs; conserved mutations in cagA, trpD, hpaA identified
comments: Genomic diversity is well-documented but functional impact of identified variants on carcinogenesis and O. viverrini co-infection remains speculative.

model_io.model: Whole-genome SNP-based phylogenetics
inputs: 12 H. pylori isolates from O. viverrini-endemic communities

hypotheses.hypothesis: H. pylori strains in liver fluke-endemic areas show adaptive evolution and strain-specific virulence patterns
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; phylogenomic clustering and cagA diversity support regional adaptation and potential contribution to hepatobiliary carcinogenesis

title: Explainable machine learning and deep learning models for predicting in-hospital mortality in burn patients
task: Explainable machine learning and deep learning for in-hospital mortality prediction in burn patients
key_results: XGBoost achieved ROC-AUC 0.9896, PR-AUC 0.9502; LightGBM and Random Forest also >0.98 ROC-AUC; SHAP, permutation importance, LIME applied for interpretability
comments: Impressive discrimination but internal validation only; external validation essential before clinical use; models intended for dynamic updating rather than static admission scoring.

model_io.model: XGBoost + gradient boosting ensemble (LightGBM, Random Forest) + neural networks
inputs: age, burn percentage, hospitalization days, ICU stay days, infection status, gender

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dynamic ensemble models with explainability improve mortality prediction during hospital course
hypotheses.result: Confirmed on internal validation; nonlinear risk patterns and patient-level behavior revealed by SHAP and LIME

title: Genetic and morphological insights reveal the hidden and colorful diversity in Oscarella sponges
task: Genomic and morphological assessment of Oscarella sponge diversity in Western Mediterranean
key_results: Identified 4 new Oscarella species; multigene phylogenetics resolved color polymorphism evolutionary scenario; highlighted limitations of cox1/COI for species resolution
comments: Combining genetic and photographic documentation is methodologically sound, but limited geographic sampling and gaps in existing genetic databases constrain global diversity estimates.

model_io.model: Multigene phylogenetics + morphological documentation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Genetic data combined with morphological documentation reveals hidden Oscarella diversity
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; identified 4 new species and highlighted cox1 limitations; standardized genetic frameworks and comprehensive datasets needed for taxon-wide resolution

title: RNA stability analysis reveals the potential involvement of endoplasmic reticulum stress in bovine endometritis
task: Identifying hub genes and pathways involved in bovine endometritis via RNA stability analysis
key_results: Brown module enriched in ER stress and immune response pathways; 28 hub genes identified including CD4, S100A4, CSF3, CCR10, KLF10; findings consistent with prior endometritis biomarkers
comments: Gene co-expression networks inferred from stability patterns are novel, but causal relationships between ER stress and endometritis require functional validation.

model_io.model: WGCNA + network propagation algorithm
inputs: RNA-Seq data from healthy and infected bovine endometrial samples

hypotheses.hypothesis: RNA stability changes distinguish endometritis-associated pathways from bulk transcriptome shifts
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; brown module shows increased RNA stability post-infection and enrichment in ER stress pathways

title: A standardized and reproducible pipeline for fast multi-view digitally reconstructed radiograph (DRR) generation
task: Standardized and reproducible pipeline for fast multi-view digitally reconstructed radiograph generation from CT
key_results: Preprocessing 1.12 s; DRR generation 5 images in 0.32 ± 0.03 s; bone-windowed projections realistic; pipeline enables standardized benchmarking for registration and synthetic imaging
comments: Pipeline is well-engineered and reproducible, but clinical utility limited; primary application to synthetic image generation, registration benchmarking, and radiographic simulation.

model_io.model: GPU-accelerated DRR generation (TIGRE cone-beam model with Beer-Lambert attenuation)
outputs: multi-view DRR images at uniformly spaced angles

hypotheses.hypothesis: Standardized preprocessing and projection framework enables reproducible DRR generation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; geometric consistency and intensity normalization achieved; realistic bone projections with flexible geometry control

title: MEE-Net: a lightweight CNN with interpretability assessment for cardiomegaly detection from chest X-rays on edge devices
task: Lightweight CNN with interpretability for cardiomegaly detection on edge devices
key_results: MEE-Net (83k parameters) achieves AUC 0.81 on both ChestX-ray8 and CheXpert; 3.5 ms CPU latency; 23.2 ms on Raspberry Pi 4; Grad-CAM maps align with anatomical regions
comments: Edge Suitability Score metric is useful but weights are arbitrary; anatomical plausibility of attention maps is preliminary without radiologist validation.

model_io.model: MEE-Net (lightweight encoder-based CNN with depthwise-separable convolutions)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Lightweight architecture achieves competitive diagnostic performance with minimal computational overhead
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; MEE-Net competitive with larger models on public benchmarks and deployable on Raspberry Pi

title: Spectral Chebyshev wavelet method for state-dependent fractional integro-differential equations in adaptive tumor growth modeling
task: Solving state-dependent fractional integro-differential equations in tumor growth models
key_results: CWOMM outperforms L1 finite-difference and spectral collocation methods; successfully models adaptive drug resistance in NSCLC xenografts
comments: Novel state-dependent kernel formulation is theoretically sound but clinical validation limited to xenograft parameters rather than patient data.

model_io.model: Chebyshev Wavelet Operational Matrix Method (CWOMM)
inputs: nonlinear mixed Volterra–Fredholm fractional integro-differential equation with state-dependent kernels
outputs: tumor growth dynamics with treatment resistance

hypotheses.hypothesis: State-dependent kernels enable modeling of acquired drug resistance
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; framework successfully reproduced adaptive treatment resistance in tumor growth model

title: Image-embedded prompt injection vulnerability of vision-language models in dental radiology: a cross-vendor attack–defense evaluation
task: Evaluating image-embedded prompt injection vulnerability and defenses in vision-language models for dental radiology
key_results: All 4 VLMs vulnerable with ASR up to 62.6% (GPT-4o); OCR-based sanitization reduced pooled ASR from 15.6% to 0.2%; ProvDent achieved 1.1% with 93.5% case coverage
comments: Stress-test conditions with permissive prompts may overstate real-world risk; cross-vendor vulnerability reproducibility is valuable but specificity assessment limited by few normal images.

model_io.model: Vision-language models (GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Claude Sonnet 4.5, MedGemma 4B) + defenses (ROI cropping, spotlighting, OCR sanitization, ProvDent)
inputs: DenTeX dental panoramic radiographs with adversarial text embedded in pixels

hypotheses.hypothesis: Vision-language models are vulnerable to image-embedded prompt injection in medical imaging
hypotheses.result: Confirmed across all 4 production-tier models; defenses effective (OCR sanitization 0.2% ASR, ProvDent 1.1%) but require human review escalation

title: Machine learning-guided screening of urine cultures for urinary tract infection diagnosis according to AMCLI guidelines
task: Automated classification and segmentation of urine culture images for UTI diagnosis
key_results: VGG-19 achieves 99.49% accuracy on test set; YOLOv11 achieves mAP@50 = 0.82 for colony detection; strongest performance on Enterobacter aerogenes and Klebsiella spp.
comments: Small dataset (115 images) and single acquisition protocol limit generalizability; multicenter validation strongly recommended before clinical deployment.

model_io.model: VGG-19 + YOLOv11 instance segmentation pipeline
outputs: individual colony masks and species classification

hypotheses.hypothesis: Deep learning can automatically screen urine cultures aligned with AMCLI guidelines
hypotheses.result: Confirmed on single-center standardized dataset; multicenter validation pending

title: Real-time gesture classification via spike trains and multi-scale temporal features from sEMG signals
task: Real-time gesture classification from sEMG signals using motor unit spike trains and temporal features
key_results: Achieves 91.02% ± 2.68% accuracy on 65-Gesture dataset; 92.06% on CSL-HDEMG; 86.63% on CapgMyo DBa; end-to-end latency <60 ms
comments: Motor unit decomposition is technically sound and enables interpretable spike-based features, but validation on diverse electrode arrays and cross-subject generalization not assessed.

model_io.model: Hybrid offline-online decomposition (CKC) + two-layer MLP classifier

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multi-scale temporal features from decomposed motor units outperform classical time-domain features
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; spike count and temporal difference features exceed Root Mean Square performance on three benchmarks

title: Brain signatures of body mass index predict cardiometabolic and respiratory disease status
task: Predicting cardiometabolic and respiratory disease status from brain BMI biomarkers derived from MRI
key_results: Brain-based models superior to BMI itself for disease detection; white matter signals in cerebellum, corpus callosum, brainstem drove predictions; tracked BMI changes over 2.3 years with stronger sensitivity to increases
comments: Intriguing finding of shared mechanisms linking metabolic state and brain structure, but cross-sectional associations do not establish causality or mechanism.

model_io.model: Deep learning on T1-weighted MRI (encoder pathway)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Brain structure biomarkers of BMI predict systemic disease status better than BMI itself
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; white matter regions (cerebellum, corpus callosum, brainstem) implicated; suggests shared metabolic-neurobiological mechanisms

title: OncoTagger: a reproducible abstract-level landscape of open-access AI-oncology articles in Web of Science
task: Evidence surveillance pipeline for AI-oncology literature landscape assessment
key_results: OncoTagger achieved 92.3% metric-detection accuracy (95% CI 88.9–95.2%), 89.3% sensitivity, 98.2% specificity on 20,766 open-access articles; 73.6% exact agreement on metric categorization
comments: Rule-based pipeline is reproducible but moderate inter-rater agreement and systematic dictionary gaps limit utility as comprehensive AI-oncology census.

model_io.model: OncoTagger rule-based abstract-level evidence-surveillance pipeline
inputs: title, abstract, keywords, metadata from Web of Science indexed articles (2019–2025)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Automated abstract-level screening can reliably categorize AI-oncology literature
hypotheses.result: Confirmed with high accuracy on metric detection but moderate agreement on task assignment; systematic gaps in dictionary coverage identified

title: Interpretable multimodal retrieval augmented diagnosis for breast ultrasound with multinational clinical validation and reader study
task: Interpretable retrieval-augmented diagnosis for breast ultrasound BI-RADS assessment
key_results: B-RAD achieves AUROC 0.952 on institutional cohort without fine-tuning; improves inter-reader agreement from moderate to substantial; reduces missed malignancies across all readers
comments: Validation across 11 cohorts from 7 countries is commendable, but training-free foveal attention mechanism adds complexity without ablation study.

model_io.model: B-RAD (retrieval-augmented diagnosis framework)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Retrieved exemplars improve lesion detection and BI-RADS classification
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; B-RAD mirrors radiologist workflow and reduces inter-observer variability

title: Shapley value explanations for clinical prediction models: a scoping review and guide
task: Systematic review and implementation guide for Shapley value explanations in clinical prediction models
key_results: 91% of publications did not disclose Shapley computation algorithm; 97% did not disclose reference population; identified four dominant use motivations

hypotheses.hypothesis: Shapley values provide transparent explanations for clinical prediction models
hypotheses.result: Confirmed in principle but hampered by inconsistent implementation and reporting practices

title: The equivalence of quantum deletion and insertion errors on permutation-invariant codes
task: Quantum insertion-deletion equivalence on permutation-invariant codes
key_results: Established conditions for t-insertion error-correction and (t,s)-insdel error-correction on permutation-invariant quantum codes; extended framework to qudit systems

hypotheses.hypothesis: Quantum insertion-deletion equivalence holds for permutation-invariant codes under specified constraints

title: Securing the open-source ecosystem: AI-enhanced and explainable supply chain security for reliable software development
task: AI-enhanced open-source supply chain security via explainable anomaly detection
key_results: XAI-SCS hybrid CNN-LSTM-Autoencoder achieved F1=0.91 on test set (F1=0.90±0.02 across 5 runs) on 12,000 npm/PyPI packages; SHAP explanations rated high clarity (4.3±0.4/5) and actionability (4.1±0.5/5); 96% self-reported remediation intent
comments: Strong anomaly detection performance on CVE-linked labels; external evaluation on 240 curated non-CVE incidents interpreted as preliminary evidence of transferability, not comprehensive coverage; optional high-assurance extensions (federated learning, zk-SNARKs) presented as exploratory, not empirically validated.

model_io.model: CNN-LSTM-Autoencoder hybrid anomaly detector
SHAP-based explainability engine

hypotheses.result: Partially confirmed; F1=0.91 on CVE-linked test set; external 240-case non-CVE evaluation interpreted as preliminary evidence, not comprehensive proof

title: Phase-aware kinematic measurement of standing long jump based on human posture vision

key_results: KSHPV achieved MAE 17.25±2.67 cm, R²=0.665±0.068 on 204 participants (219 trials); phase alignment improved explanatory power ΔR²=0.289; outperformed anthropometrics-only baseline (MAE 28.92 cm, R²=0.160)

title: Application of an integrated IDOCRIW-Copeland MCDM framework for ranking agro-based natural fibers
task: Multi-criteria evaluation of agro-based natural fibers via integrated IDOCRIW-Copeland MCDM
key_results: Coir ranked first; Jute and Hemp in 2nd/3rd; Spearman rank correlation ρ=1.00 among TOPSIS/VIKOR/EDAS; consensus achieved via Copeland meta-ranking
comments: Comprehensive nine-criterion evaluation across physical-chemical-mechanical properties; transferability to fiber variant selection within same species unexamined.

Copeland meta-ranking aggregator

hypotheses.hypothesis: Copeland meta-ranking yields stable consensus across diverse MCDM methods
